edges.description: Reduced cortical neuron output gives a small brain and head from birth.
A smaller cortical sheet forms fewer and simpler gyri in some patients.
Fewer cortical neurons project fewer axons, consistent with the global reduction in white matter seen on imaging.
Ventricular enlargement accompanies the global reduction in white matter volume rather than reflecting obstruction.
Reduced cortical neuron number underlies the neurodevelopmental impairment.
Seizures occur in a minority of patients on the background of the small cortex.
The constitutive null does not reproduce congenital microcephaly; its dominant brain phenotype is a neuronal migration defect that human MCPH27 imaging does not show.
edges.limitations: A homozygous null allele, whereas MCPH27 is caused by heterozygous missense variants proposed to act dominantly on lamin assembly; heterozygous Lmnb2+/- mice are phenotypically normal. The model is closer to the biallelic loss-of-function human phenotype (PMID:40011009).

nodes.description: Heterozygous missense variants alter conserved residues in coiled-coil segments of the lamin B2 alpha-helical rod: Asn54 at the coil 1A intradimer interface and Glu398 at the coil 2B intradimer interface. Glu398 normally repels the Glu398 of the partner chain; the p.Glu398Lys substitution is predicted by structural modeling on lamin A/C structures to aberrantly stabilize mixed mutant/wild-type dimers. The variants are proposed to act dominantly on assembly of the lamin B2 filament that forms part of the nuclear lamina, rather than by haploinsufficiency.

genetic_context.description: Recurrent de novo missense variants at specific residues and the absence of truncating variants led the reporting authors to favor a dominant negative mechanism (with gain of function not excluded) over haploinsufficiency. This is an inference from the variant spectrum and structural modeling, not a measured effect on endogenous lamin B2.

nodes.description: Lamin B2-null mice die shortly after birth with a lissencephaly-like neuronal layering defect in the cerebral cortex and cerebellum caused by defective neuronal migration, while brain size at birth is nearly normal.

The reporting authors propose that LMNB2 variants alter the physical properties of lamin filaments, making the nuclei of neural progenitors fragile under the mechanical stresses of interkinetic nuclear migration and neuronal migration and increasing cell death during brain development. The proposal rests on the analogous LMNA variant producing fragile nuclei; increased apoptosis in the cortex has been observed in lamin B2-null mouse embryos, but not with the human variants.

nodes.description: B-type lamins associate with the mitotic spindle, and mice lacking B-type lamins show defects in spindle orientation in neural progenitor cells. The reporting authors propose this as the mechanism of LMNB1/LMNB2 microcephaly, in line with the spindle defects of other primary microcephaly genes. The evidence comes from null mice, not from the heterozygous human missense variants.
